chunks: Tell them: 'Leaving God aside, will you worship something that has no power over your loss or gain?' But God is all-hearing and all-knowing.

key_terms.مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ: Aside from God / In place of God

ai.seo_question: Why do polytheists worship idols if they cannot help or harm?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Ma'idah, this verse critiques the polytheists' reliance on lifeless idols that lack the divine attributes of agency, contrasting them with Allah who is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. Shia exegesis often highlights this as a foundational argument for Tawhid (monotheism), emphasizing that true intercession or benefit comes only from God, thereby refuting the notion of independent power in created objects. The verse serves as a direct challenge to those who attribute divine qualities to entities that are merely inert and dependent.
